blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (One customer query per invoice in the monthly report) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
fn customer_label(db: &dyn Db, invoice: &Invoice) -> Result<String, DbError> {
    let customer = db.customer(invoice.customer_id)?;
findings.recommendation: `customer_label` is called for every invoice in the loop of `monthly_report` (`src/report.rs:23-26`), so it runs `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1` once per invoice: with the proposal's ~3 000 invoices a month from 800 customers, one report issues ~3 000 customer queries (cost grows linearly with the month's invoices, and repeats each customer ~4 times). `Db::customers(&[i64])` (`src/db.rs:26`, `WHERE id = ANY($1)`) already serves the whole set: collect the distinct `customer_id`s, fetch them in one call, index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>`, and build each line from the map. Keep the invoice-number order and return a `DbError` when a customer is missing, as today.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

findings.evidence:
fn purchase_order(notes: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let pattern = Regex::new(r"PO-\d{4}-\d{4}").expect("a valid pattern");
findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice of the month (`src/report.rs:28`), so `Regex::new` compiles the same pattern ~3 000 times per report; compiling a pattern is expensive compared with matching one short note. Compile it once — a `static PATTERN: LazyLock<Regex>` (or `once_cell::sync::Lazy`), or build it in `monthly_report` and pass it in.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
